title: KV cache lease-breach chain recovery and graceful repopulation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a capacity surge on 2026-02-18 a subset of KV cache shards entered a 'lease-breach' state where held leases were not released after eviction decisions, causing cascading repopulation stalls, high memory retention and client tail-latency spikes. Unlike prior poisoning incidents, the root cause ties to a race between lease renewal, eviction scoring, and the async repopulation worker that re-creates entries without validating lease ownership. Impact: ~8% of requests saw >500ms tail latency for 90 minutes, two Dedicated customers reported degraded throughput and one internal rate-limiter tripped. Scope: affects prefix-based KV shards on kernels with async-compact enabled and repopulation workers on Linux kernels >=5.18. Goals: 1) Provide an immediate mitigation to stop cascading repopulation storms; 2) Implement a durable reconciliation and guardrail plan to prevent lease-breach races; 3) Add observability and automated remediation to shorten MTTR for similar events.
action_items: TEMP_MITIGATE: Add lease validation in repopulation worker (check lease owner + lease epoch) — owner: Marco Gutiérrez — due: 2026-03-05
RECONCILER: Implement periodic shard reconciler that clears stale leases when consensus TTL exceeded and publishes reconciliation events — owner: Li Wei — due: 2026-03-19
BACKPRESSURE: Add per-shard repopulation backoff and global circuit-breaker to limit simultaneous reconstructions — owner: Priya Nair — due: 2026-03-22
TESTING: Add deterministic race integration test against lease renew / eviction / repopulation interleavings — owner: Owen Martinez — due: 2026-03-18
INSTRUMENTATION: Surface lease state, lease-owner, lease-epoch, and repopulation queue length in Console per-route dashboards — owner: SRE Team (oncall lead: Ravi Singh) — due: 2026-03-12
CANARY: Canary rollout plan for runtime-1.24 with canary cohort 2% then 10% then 50% with 24h observation windows — owner: Release Eng (contact: Dana Kim) — due: 2026-03-26
POSTMORTEM_DOC: Publish final incident write-up and link action-item completions in Confluence — owner: Aisha Patel — due: 2026-03-28
comments: 2026-02-18 09:24 — initial pager: high latency cluster A. Triage by oncall (Marco). Noticed repopulation worker storms on shard 17. Captured heap profiles and KV metrics.

2026-02-18 10:03 — hypothesis: repopulation is recreating entries despite eviction because lease ownership not validated. Temporary mitigation applied: paused repopulation workers for shard groups 15-20. Immediate latency improved.
2026-02-18 12:11 — telemetry: prefixcache.alive_entries decreased by 22% but memory did not reduce due to orphaned lease structures. Investigated async-compact interactions.

2026-02-19 08:44 — root cause narrowed: race between lease renewal path and eviction scoring path causes lease epoch to get out-of-sync; repopulation worker absent check on lease epoch so it overwrote/retained objects resulting in logical memory churn.

2026-02-22 16:05 — design decision: implement 2-phase repopulation (validate lease owner and epoch, then CAS-insert) + periodic reconciler. Reviewed with runtime and SRE teams. Agreed to prioritize a temporary fix in runtime-1.24 then follow with reconciler.

2026-02-28 11:27 — PR opened: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/6448 — 'repopulate: validate lease owner & epoch before insert' — assigned to Marco. Unit tests added. Noted potential perf cost; added metrics to measure validation latency.

2026-03-02 09:52 — code-review feedback: Priya requested an opt-out flag for environments where strict validation causes regressions; added 'repopulate.strict_lease_validation' config (default=true for hosted).

2026-03-05 14:19 — TEMP_MITIGATE deployed to hosted regions eu-west-1 and us-east-1 behind runtime-1.24-canary. Early signals: 60% reduction in repopulation queue depth and no tail-latency regressions observed in 24h.
2026-03-09 10:40 — reconciler design doc drafted: confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/KV+Lease+Reconciler — includes idempotent reconciler steps and event schema. Link shared with SRE/PM.

2026-03-11 15:03 — integration test checklist: add deterministic fuzzing harness to reproduce lease-breach on CI. Owen to pair with Marco. Blocking: need infra quota for heavier CI runs (ticket INFRA-872).
2026-03-12 09:00 — blockers: finalizing the per-shard backpressure algorithm; risk assessment shows aggressive backpressure can increase cold-miss rate. Planning calibration run during canary.

2026-03-12 17:45 — next steps: finish reconciler prototype, land backpressure feature behind feature flag, and schedule canary for 2026-03-17. Aisha will coordinate customer communication for affected Dedicated customers.
status_notes: Temporary mitigation applied in canary and showing positive signals. Main blocking area: calibrating per-shard backpressure to avoid cold-miss regressions. Reconciler prototype in review.
